title: UCP business profile
question: Does the merchant publish a Universal Commerce Protocol profile?
method: GET /.well-known/ucp. Pass on 200 JSON whose ucp object carries a version in YYYY-MM-DD form and services and payment_handlers objects (both may be empty). Warn when the profile is served after a redirect or without Cache-Control public with max-age of at least 60 seconds (the specification forbids redirects and requires that caching), when it is served with an HTML content type (this scanner's heuristic for a page standing in for the document), or when a profile declaring version 2026-08-25 still carries signing_keys instead of keys. A refusal or challenge on the profile URL is reported as such, not as absence. Fail when absent or not JSON. Shopify serves this profile for every eligible Online Store; Google Merchant Center requires it for agentic checkout and its guides still target version 2026-04-08.

title: UCP checkout capability and payment handler
question: Does the UCP profile declare a checkout an agent could use?
method: From the profile: pass when a dev.ucp.shopping.checkout capability or a dev.ucp.shopping service with a rest, mcp or a2a transport is declared and at least one payment handler carries id, version and spec; warn when only one of the two is present; fail when neither. When a rest service names an endpoint, GET it and record the status: 404 or 5xx adds a warning, because the agent would fail there.

title: ACP discovery document
question: Does the merchant advertise an Agentic Commerce Protocol integration?
method: GET /.well-known/acp.json. Pass on JSON with protocol.name "acp", a protocol.version, an api_base_url and a transports array that includes rest; record supported_versions and capabilities. Fail when absent. The document is a merged proposal in the ACP repository (status proposal, version unreleased, not part of the released 2026-04-17 specification), and OpenAI does not document probing it; checkout endpoints are registered with the platform privately, so this is the only public trace and the weight is low.

title: ACP feed fields
question: If the public feed follows the OpenAI format, does it carry the seller and return fields a checkout needs?
method: When B1.5 found a JSON, CSV or TSV feed with OpenAI-style columns, read sampled items. Pass when seller_name, return_policy and return_deadline_in_days (alias return_window) are present, or seller_privacy_policy and seller_tos (required for checkout) are; warn when only seller_name is; fail when none. Skip as not applicable for Google-format XML feeds, which have no such fields.

title: Guest checkout and cart API
question: Can an agent build a cart without an account?
method: GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart must respond 200 with a cart object. Warn when the checkout page requires login (guest checkout disabled).

title: Shopify agentic storefront active
question: Is the Shopify store exposing its agent surface?
method: For Shopify Online Store storefronts: pass when responses carry Link: </.well-known/ucp>; rel="ucp" (or the HTML link element) and a JSON-RPC server/discover POST to /api/ucp/mcp is answered with a JSON-RPC message (an authorization failure arrives as a JSON-RPC error, not a 401), which means the Agentic storefronts channel is active and its catalog tools are reachable; warn when only one of the two holds, or when the scanner did not call the endpoint because robots.txt disallows /api/ for its user agent; fail when neither holds. The channel is active by default for eligible stores, so a fail means ineligibility or opt-out. A headless storefront (Shopify assets but no Shopify-served origin) gets neither the profile nor the endpoint on its own domain and is not judged here.
